title: Highlights limitation statement
text: Highlights begin with the verbatim limitation statement naming the product: "These highlights do not include all the information needed to use [PROPRIETARY NAME] safely and effectively. See full prescribing information for [PROPRIETARY NAME]."

title: Product title
text: The product title gives the proprietary name, the established name, the dosage form and the route of administration, plus the controlled substance symbol where one applies.

title: Initial U.S. Approval
text: Highlights state "Initial U.S. Approval:" and the four-digit year the active moiety was first approved in the US.

title: Boxed warning in Highlights
text: When the full prescribing information has a boxed warning, Highlights carry a summary: a heading starting "WARNING:", no more than 20 lines, ending with "See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning."
simplified: The 20-line limit is estimated from the text length (about 65 characters per line in the two-column layout).

title: Recent Major Changes
text: Recent Major Changes list substantive changes to the Boxed Warning, Indications and Usage, Dosage and Administration, Contraindications, or Warnings and Precautions only, each with the section heading, number and the month and year of the change. An entry stays for at least one year and is removed at the first printing after that year.
simplified: The app flags entries older than 12 months before the revision date. In practice an entry may stay until the next printing after the year ends.

title: Highlights cite their sections
text: Each statement in Highlights is followed by the number of the section or subsection in the full prescribing information that it summarises, in parentheses, for example "(5.2)".
simplified: Checked for bullets and paragraphs under Indications, Dosage and Administration, Dosage Forms, Contraindications, Warnings and Precautions, Adverse Reactions, Drug Interactions and Use in Specific Populations.

title: Adverse reaction contact statement
text: The Adverse Reactions heading in Highlights includes "To report SUSPECTED ADVERSE REACTIONS, contact [name of manufacturer] at [phone] or FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch."

title: Patient counselling statement
text: Highlights end with "See 17 for PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION", adding "and Medication Guide" or "and FDA-approved patient labeling" when patient labeling exists.

title: Revision date
text: Highlights show the date of the most recent revision as "Revised: MM/YYYY".

title: Highlights length
text: Highlights, not counting the boxed warning, fit on one-half page in the required two-column layout. A waiver may be requested.
simplified: Estimated: about 76 lines of 65 characters, counting each heading as a line. Real length depends on the typeset page.

title: Contraindications match
text: Every contraindication in section 4 is summarised in Highlights; "None" in section 4 is "None" in Highlights.
simplified: Compared by count of items: each list item or paragraph in section 4 should have a matching Highlights item.

title: Required sections have content
text: Sections 1 to 6, 8 (with 8.1, 8.2, 8.4 and 8.5), 11, 12 (with 12.1 and 12.3), 16 and 17 are required in PLR format; 7, 10, 13 and 14 are expected for most products. Section and subsection numbers never change, even when one is omitted.
simplified: Sections marked recommended are a warning when empty; the regulation allows them to be omitted when not applicable.

title: Exact headings
text: Section and fixed subsection headings use the wording set by the regulation, for example "8.4 Pediatric Use", not "8.4 Pediatrics".

title: Contraindications never left blank
text: Section 4 lists each contraindication, or states "None." when there are none.

title: Cross-references resolve
text: Every cross-reference in parentheses, for example "[see Warnings and Precautions (5.3)]", points to a section or subsection that exists.

title: Boxed warning points to section 5
text: The boxed warning in the full prescribing information refers to the Warnings and Precautions subsection(s) where the risk is discussed in more detail.

title: Pregnancy and lactation (PLLR)
text: Section 8.1 Pregnancy and 8.2 Lactation each include a "Risk Summary". The letter categories (A, B, C, D, X) were removed by the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule and must not appear.

title: Clinical trials statement in section 6
text: When section 6 presents clinical trial data, it includes the standard statement that adverse reaction rates from different trials cannot be compared directly.

title: Strengths agree
text: The strengths in Highlights (Dosage Forms and Strengths), section 3, section 16 and the product record are the same.

title: Section 17 points to patient labelling
text: When a Medication Guide or other FDA-approved patient labeling exists, section 17 tells the prescriber to advise the patient to read it.

title: Established name spelled consistently
text: The established name is spelled the same way everywhere. Near-misses (one or two letters different) are usually typing errors.
simplified: Detects words within two letters of the established name.

title: No trailing zeros
text: Doses and strengths never carry a trailing zero ("5 mg", not "5.0 mg"): the decimal point can be missed and a tenfold overdose given.

title: No naked decimals
text: Doses below 1 always carry a leading zero ("0.5 mg", not ".5 mg").

title: No error-prone abbreviations
text: Avoid abbreviations on the ISMP error-prone list, for example U or IU for units, QD, QOD, SC or SQ, cc, and ug for micrograms.
simplified: A subset of the ISMP list is checked.

title: Patient labelling headings
text: Patient labelling uses the required headings in order, in question form, with the product name filled in, and each required heading has content.
simplified: Headings follow the FDA templates; the PPI and IFU headings are recommended practice rather than regulation.

title: Patient labelling statements
text: A Medication Guide is titled "MEDICATION GUIDE", gives the side-effect reporting statement, states that it has been approved by FDA, and shows the revision date.

title: Most important information matches the boxed warning
text: When the prescribing information has a boxed warning, the Medication Guide opens with the most important information on that risk.

title: Reading level
text: Patient labelling is written in plain language. The app estimates a reading grade and flags long sentences and medical terms with lay alternatives.
simplified: Flesch-Kincaid grade estimate in English; a hint only, never a pass or fail.

title: Required label particulars
text: Carton and container labels carry the proprietary and established names, strength, dosage form, net quantity, "Rx only", NDC, lot number, expiration date and the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor; cartons also carry the route, a dosage statement and storage.

title: NDC format
text: The NDC is 10 digits in one of the configurations 4-4-2, 5-3-2 or 5-4-1.

title: Bar code
text: Prescription drug labels carry a linear bar code that contains the NDC.

title: Established name prominence
text: The established name is printed in letters at least half as large as the letters of the proprietary name, with prominence commensurate with it.

title: Strength matches the PI
text: The strength on the carton or container is one of the strengths in the approved prescribing information.

title: Strength per total volume and per mL
text: For injectables, the strength is shown as the amount per total volume, followed by the amount per mL (for example "50 mg/5 mL (10 mg/mL)").

title: Medication Guide statement
text: When a Medication Guide is required, the carton tells the dispenser to provide it: "Dispense the accompanying Medication Guide to each patient."

title: Same as the reference label
text: Generic labeling is the same as the reference listed drug labeling, except for permitted differences: for example the manufacturer, inactive ingredients, how supplied, and indications omitted because of patents or exclusivity.

title: Biosimilarity statement and footnote
text: The Highlights of a biosimilar carry the biosimilarity statement "[BIOSIMILAR] ([proper name]) is biosimilar* to [REFERENCE PRODUCT] ([proper name])", with a footnote explaining that biosimilar means highly similar to the FDA-approved reference product with no clinically meaningful differences, and for which conditions of use biosimilarity was shown.
at: FDA labeling guidance for biosimilar products (2018, revised draft 2023)
simplified: The app checks for the statement with both names and the key phrases of the footnote.

title: The biosimilar is described by its own name
text: Statements about the biosimilar use its own proprietary and proper name (with the four-letter suffix). The reference product's brand name appears only in the biosimilarity statement.
at: FDA labeling guidance for biosimilar products
simplified: Simplified: the guidance also covers when to use the core name for data from studies of the reference product; the app only looks for the reference brand name outside the statement.

title: Interchangeability statement (Watch)
text: The September 2023 revised draft guidance no longer recommends an interchangeability statement in labeling; interchangeability is shown in the Purple Book. Shown as a hint until the guidance is final.

title: Carve-outs are complete
text: When a protected indication is carved out under section viii, every mention that depends on it is removed: the indication, its dosing, its clinical studies and its Highlights entries.
simplified: Mentions are found by keywords defined for each indication in the exercise.
